product_overview: A Next.js frontend for ForgeGraph that provides user authentication, company creation and operation flows, operation monitoring, operational pages for prompts/credentials/approvals/memory, and admin/analytics surfaces. The app surfaces backend-driven company state and operating models to end users.
core_goals: Create and configure AI-driven companies and their operating models
Start, inspect, and monitor company operations and view detailed traces and memory activity
Manage prompts, credentials, human approvals, and stored memory observations
Authenticate and access protected app surfaces and onboarding flows
View analytics and admin screens to monitor usage, billing, and workspace access settings

features.name: Authentication and Session Flows
features.description: Allow users to register, sign in, and access protected pages; unauthenticated attempts are redirected to authentication entry points.
user_flows: Navigate to /register -> Fill email and password fields -> Submit registration -> See /login?registered=true and the registration-success message -> Sign in with the new account -> See protected pages available

Navigate to /login -> Fill email and password fields on login or registration forms -> Submit credentials and wait for navigation into the authenticated app -> Land on /companies and use the current shell navigation to reach company workspaces or advanced operating-model routes as needed
Navigate to /login -> Fill email and password fields with incorrect credentials -> Submit credentials -> See validation error indicating invalid credentials

features.name: Advanced Operating Model Authoring
features.description: Provide an advanced visual editor for creating and editing operating models, configuring steps, running validation overlays, and using wizards to scaffold content.
user_flows: Navigate to /workflows or /graphs -> Open an advanced operating model from the list -> Add steps -> Connect steps -> Open step configuration forms -> Edit step settings and model metadata -> Trigger validation -> See validation overlay indicating pass -> Save the operating model

Navigate to /workflows or /graphs -> Open an advanced operating model from the list -> Add a step with incomplete configuration -> Trigger validation -> See validation errors in overlay -> Open step configuration forms -> Fix step configuration -> Trigger validation -> See validation overlay indicating pass -> Save the operating model

features.name: Operation Monitoring and Feedback
features.description: List past and active operations, surface operation statuses, traces, and memory activity, and let users inspect operation details.
user_flows: Navigate to /runs -> Browse operation list to find work of interest -> Select an operation to view its detailed trace and status -> Observe operation statuses, traces, and memory activity panels
Navigate to /runs -> Browse operation list -> Select an operation to view detail -> Refresh or revisit the operation detail to observe updated status and trace entries

features.name: Prompt, Credential, Approval, and Memory Management
features.description: Operational pages for browsing, inspecting, creating, and updating prompts, credentials, approvals, and stored memory observations. Memory observations are currently inspect-only in the UI, and credential metadata editing is not exposed.
user_flows: Navigate to /prompts -> Browse list of prompts -> Open a prompt detail -> Edit prompt content and submit -> See updated prompt in the list
Navigate to /credentials -> Browse credential list or empty state -> Inspect OAuth integration and connection checklist actions
Navigate to /inbox -> Browse pending approvals -> Submit Approve or Reject when a pending approval exists -> See the inbox posture remain visible or the empty state when no items are pending
Navigate to /memory -> Browse memory observations -> Open an observation detail -> Inspect captured content without tag or metadata edit controls

features.name: Analytics, Onboarding, and Admin Surfaces
features.description: Dashboards and admin interfaces for onboarding progress, LLM and memory analytics, billing, workspace access, SSO, audit logs, marketplace, and operations.
user_flows: Navigate to /onboarding -> Review backend-driven onboarding checklist progress and labels; do not assume an incomplete milestone exists
Navigate to /analytics/llm -> Review AI access usage charts and metrics -> Navigate to /analytics/memory -> Review knowledge usage charts and metrics
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/billing -> Review billing and plan information
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/organization -> Inspect workspace access settings and members
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/audit-logs -> Review recent audit entries
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/marketplace -> Inspect marketplace packages and administration controls
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/operations -> Inspect operational controls and diagnostics
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/sso -> Inspect SSO configuration and status
Navigate to /admin -> Navigate to /admin/help -> Review admin support and help resources

routes.description: Marketing landing page and entry point to login or app flows.
Advanced operating model listing page. The authenticated shell may expose this area through an Advanced navigation label.
Graph editor page for creating and editing workflow graphs.
Detailed run trace and status page.
Memory browser and observation management page.
Human approval inbox page. The legacy /approvals page reuses the same implementation.

features.name: Authentication and Session Flows
features.description: Register, login, protected routing, and callback handling for authenticated app access.
user_interactions: Fill email and password fields on login or registration forms.
Submit registration and expect redirect to /login?registered=true before signing in.
Submit login credentials and wait for navigation into the authenticated app.
Attempt to open a protected page and get redirected when unauthenticated.
Return from OAuth or SSO callback routes and complete login flow.

features.name: Graph Authoring Experience
features.description: Advanced operating-model editing, step configuration, validation overlays, and wizard-assisted authoring. In the current shell, entry is surfaced as Advanced.
user_interactions: Open the graph list and navigate into a graph editor.
Add nodes, connect edges, and open node configuration forms.
Edit graph metadata and node settings.
Trigger validation and inspect overlay or status feedback.
Use the agent wizard and quick-add tools to scaffold graph content.

features.name: Operation Monitoring and Feedback
features.description: Operator-facing operation pages, operation history, trace detail, and event-driven status views.
user_interactions: Open the operation list to inspect previous work.
Navigate to a specific operation detail page.
Observe operation statuses, traces, and memory activity panels.
Refresh or revisit operation detail after backend status changes.

features.name: Prompt, Credential, Approval, and Memory Management
features.description: Operational pages for prompts, credentials, human approvals, and stored memory observations. Prompt editing and approval decisions are interactive; memory observations are inspect-only; credential metadata editing is not exposed.
user_interactions: Open prompt, credential, approval, or memory pages from the app navigation.
Browse lists, inspect detail panels, and submit only currently exposed forms.
Review pending approvals and inspect memory observations without making the client authoritative for durable state.

features.name: Analytics, Onboarding, and Admin Surfaces
features.description: Dashboards and administration pages for analytics, onboarding progress, billing, workspace access, SSO, audit logs, operations, and marketplace views.
user_interactions: Open onboarding and analytics dashboards after login.
Navigate through admin sections and inspect workspace access, billing, SSO, audit, and marketplace pages.
Review charts, tables, and status cards driven by backend data.

known_limitations.issue: Most meaningful routes depend on authenticated backend APIs and seeded data.
known_limitations.impact: Frontend-only tests need mocks, while end-to-end tests need backend and engine support to exercise real flows.

known_limitations.issue: The graph editor is interaction-heavy and sensitive to API and validation responses.
known_limitations.impact: High-confidence coverage requires integration or E2E tests in addition to simple component rendering tests.
